The board in question

So, as the title says, I want to have not only two more COM ports, but one more parallel port to use in my workshop computer. There are footprints for resistors and capacitors on the PCB, but I'm not sure what ratings do they have to be.

I'm pretty sure capacitors can be of any low value, as they are just for filtering noise, but what about the resistors?
What resistors / capacitors do I need to be able to use parallel port on this card?

Where did you find the card ? without having the circuit handy its going to take you some google foo to find the data sheet for that chip labeled "moschip" if your lucky the data sheet will have a reference circuit for you to make educated guesses from

Failing that its possible they may just be pull up or pull down resistors and in most cases they are 10k ohms but look it up for parallel ports cause im too lazy to google that for you.

It's from retired parts box in my university. I couldn't find any reference circuits in chip's datasheet or any high quality photos of the card version with parallel port to read the resistor markings.

Some resistors are between output pins (current limiters?) and some between pins and ground (pulldowns).

again i can't read anything with the potato quality writing on the chip my best guess is it MOSCHP mcs9865 and im thinking the reference circuit from http://www.asix.com.tw/products.php?op=pItemdetail&PItemID=125;74;111& may be close enough to give you an idea.

that said if there were better photos of the chip you may get better responses
however check out the reference circuit for the parallel port it looks like some are 4.7Kohm , 33 ohm, and some are dead shorts

the 33 ohms likely will be for current limiting as they are inline for the D0-D7 pins and some of the control lines. (33ohms will be linked to the resistance current (i should not drink and type) the device can sink or source )

The 4.7Kohms will be pullups and appear to be on all lines in the reference circuit i found. ACKN BUSY ERROR and SELECT lines all appear to use dead shorts you can buy 0ohm resistors or drag solder to bridge those connections if they arn't already

your caps are all 180pF which is small and they are likely for filtering as you suspected the value was likely chosen so the draining or filling of the capacitor will not affect signalling when it is switching at its fastest rate. (signals faster than that will be averaged out by the cap)

good luck

For justifying your purchases explain it is your hobby and your money. Your partner should be allowed the same freedom to persue their hobby.

I'd say the question is less how I justify being a PC gamer, and more how I'm gonna be able to justify getting a PS4 just to play The Last Guardian.

Quite simple:

How much does an X1 or PS4 cost? $350 on Amazon for an X1 right now. Ok. Now the reality is the average adult needs a desktop anyways. So if you need a desktop + mkb + monitor you're talking about $400 at least at your average big box store (Costco, Walmart, etc.).

Now if you do actual work on your PC you at least need a few gigs of RAM + a decent processor. So you're talking more there but that's not even necessary to factor in at this point. Really when it comes down to it, for the average adult, the only extra expense in a gaming PC is the GPU/MOBO, arguably a higher end PSU. You can get an R9 285 for under $200 and that's cheaper than an Xbox One/PS4. Once you factor in cheaper games there is no real "extra" expense at all, you make it up on software savings.

I built both of my last two gaming desktops for under $600 a piece and I could have spent less on my second if I wanted to, I wish I had but I bought into hype. I used stock Dell MKB sets until finally spending some bucks on a mech kb and a nice gaming mouse but those aren't necessary purchases.
Take your numbers, and add a dozen games, and suddenly the pc is cheaper anyway.

I do a lot of intensive tasks on my PC so in general I need good hardware. The only thing that comes close to being gaming specific is my graphics card and even then I do video and photo editing with Adobe products so I used that to justify upgrading my graphics card from my old one last year.

I've had my current desktop for three years I think and it should last me quite a bit longer. By comparison I've owned three PS1s, 2 PS2s, and I currently own a PS3 with a bad optical drive.

My optical drive breaks on my PC I can replace it in 5 minutes for less than $20 and I don't really need it anyways. My PS3 still runs and I only really use it for three games so it's fine for me but that dead optical drive would mean a new PS3 to most console gamers.

Every time I go back to playing on console I am reminded why I play on PC.

That's how.

I program so I need a computer obviously, but not just that, I do watch what I spend on my PC and I haven't gone over my limit.

I work out my limit by looking at the cost of a console (~£329) then the cost of the online service(~£30) and then the fact that I would still need a PC anyway so I factor in the cost of a half decent pre-built (~£400) and now it becomes worth it because instead of comparing my PC to consoles only, I've looked at it from both a utility and a gaming perspective, allowing myself ~£759 to spend and I still haven't spent that much on my PC, making it, in my opinion, cheaper than buying console because of what I'm getting out of it.

For me you have to remember hay having a pc isn't just for gaming. By having two monitors I've allowed to increase my uni work output and make it a more pleasant experience.

I don't even game much anymore but have for heavily into anime and manga. Where do I watch it? On my pc ofcourse with it bumped up to 60fps when I can.

So overall not only do I get enjoyment from gaming, I get it through other mediums by using my pc. Also I think at least basic knowledge of how to build a pc is a skill in itself.
I will spend less in an upgrade cycle of my PC than I would on a console because of the price of games and free online services.

I want this, I will spend my money on it.

What's to justify?

Why would I have to justify anything? I don't want to go all "PCMR", but PC is the superior platform.
From a strictly gaming perspective, yes the PC is more expensive when you first buy it and you probably have to upgrade the videocard ever 3 years or so. But in the long run it will be cheaper when you account for cheaper games and backwards compatibility. With some fiddling, I could probably play any game ever released on PC (dosbox etc). Also, on PC you can get mods for games, this fact alone blows consoles away.
However, the PC is not just for gaming, it's for everything. School / Work projects, movies, TV-series, the web (VOAT), photo and video editing, programming, banking, online shopping, multitasking (like watching a movie on one screen while playing a game or browsing the web on the other), etc, etc. Consoles can do some of these things, but most not as good as PC and some not at all.
There is no contest. PC wins.
You will never, ever need to justify your hobby. It's a HOBBY. Its only use is to waste time and resources.

I haven't bought new parts in 4 years now. I never buy any games that are not at least 75% discount. Honestly enough the only part i need to update in the next 4 years is the grahics card and maybe another HD and memory.

In my case it was and remains much cheaper. I love gaming, and have since I was a child playing Atari games with my dad. By the end of the PS2 era I was buying a new title a week, and often two or three cheap used games as well. The breakdown when added up was something like $85 dollars a week I was spending on games, peripherals, guides and collectibles. I literally stopped by game stop every Friday after getting paid.

Around the same time as the PS3 was released I tried World of Warcraft again after a year of not playing and found a great group of people to run with. I decided to go PC and just skip the consoles, and that was that. For most of the last decade I averaged between $200-$600 dollars on hardware a year to keep my moderately high end gaming system current, and $180-$540 on game subscriptions (At one point I subbed to WoW, Tera and FFXI.) That's a savings of about 3k a year even on the years I shelled out for a new top of the line card. Now I pay for no subs because of WoW tokens and everything else I play is free to play or free on Kongregate, Negrounds etc. Occasionally I buy the humble bundles for 5 dollars apiece, and just from that I have more standalone titles in my Steam library than I could finish in a lifetime.

tldr: PC gaming, for my specific wants and needs anyway, has been hugely cheaper, given me more titles for less money, and has connected me to some awesome people from around the world.

It's cheaper than console gaming if your upgrade standard is something like "play at High settings or better" or "don't fall behind consoles", instead of staying in the top 1% of gaming PCs.

I spend $1400 on the PC and by the time I find myself bumping settings down to Medium in new games, it's been 6 years. Even at a conservative, rounded-down average of 6 games per year, 1400 + (28 * 6 * 6) = $2408. The console gamer? 350 + (60 * 6 * 6) = $2510.

Raise the number of games purchased above the average, or account for the average console gamer actually buying 2 consoles per generation, and the difference in cost grows truly crazy.
